summary: Login/session behavior fully characterized. Multiple authentication vulnerabilities identified including SQL injection login bypass, mass assignment admin registration, weak password reset with exposed security questions, CSRF-vulnerable GET-based password change, non-expiring JWT tokens containing sensitive data, no logout endpoint, and insecure direct object references in basket API. Auth issues have proof_excerpt candidates with verbatim tool output.

candidates.title: SQL Injection in Login - Authentication Bypass
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST with payload {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"test"} returned 200 with body containing "authentication":{"token":"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..."} and "umail":"admin@juice-sh.op", proving SQL injection login bypass as admin user.
candidates.poc_hint: SQL injection in email field of login form. Payload: ' OR 1=1--

candidates.title: Mass Assignment - Admin Registration
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST with {"email":"massadmin@test.com","password":"test123","role":"admin"} returned 201 with body containing "role":"admin", proving mass assignment allows registering as admin without authentication.
candidates.poc_hint: Include "role":"admin" in POST body to /api/Users to create admin account

candidates.title: Weak Captcha - Answer Exposed in Response
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/captcha returned {"captchaId":0,"captcha":"1+3+3","answer":"7"} exposing the answer directly in the response, allowing automated captcha bypass.
candidates.poc_hint: Captcha answer is returned alongside the question, easily bypassed

candidates.title: Security Question Exposed for Any User
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op returned {"question":{"id":2,"question":"Mother's maiden name?"}} leaking security questions for any email without authentication.
candidates.poc_hint: Leaks security question for any email, aiding brute-force password reset

candidates.title: Password Reset via Security Question - Bjoern's Account
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST with {"email":"bjoern@owasp.org","answer":"Zaya","new":"test123","repeat":"test123"} returned 200 with user data including password hash, proving password reset with known security answer works.
candidates.poc_hint: Security question answer 'Zaya' for bjoern@owasp.org enables password reset (OSINT challenge)

candidates.title: Password Change via GET Request (CSRF)
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/user/change-password?current=admin123&new=newpass&repeat=newpass with Authorization header returned 200 with updated user object containing new password hash, proving password can be changed via GET request (CSRF vulnerable).
candidates.poc_hint: Password change via GET query parameters - no CSRF token required

candidates.title: JWT Token Contains Sensitive Data (Password Hash)
candidates.proof_excerpt: Decoded JWT payload: {"data":{"id":1,"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","password":"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500","role":"admin",...}} - JWT token exposes password hash and role in plaintext.
candidates.poc_hint: JWT token decodes to reveal password hashes, roles, and other sensitive user data

candidates.title: JWT Token Has No Expiration
candidates.proof_excerpt: JWT payload contains only "iat":1784853679 (issued at) with no "exp" claim, meaning tokens never expire and remain valid indefinitely.
candidates.poc_hint: Tokens have no expiry - stolen tokens can be used forever

candidates.title: No Logout Endpoint - Token Cannot Be Invalidated
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /rest/user/logout returned 500 "Unexpected path: /rest/user/logout" - no server-side logout mechanism exists; tokens cannot be invalidated after compromise.
candidates.poc_hint: No logout functionality - tokens remain valid forever

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure - User API
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /api/Users with admin JWT returned all users including password hashes (e.g. "password":"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500"), email addresses, roles, and other PII for all users.
candidates.poc_hint: Authenticate as admin via SQLi login bypass then access /api/Users

candidates.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference - BasketItems API
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /api/BasketItems with any valid JWT returned all basket items for all users including BasketId 1 through 5, showing no access control filtering by user's own basket.
candidates.poc_hint: Any authenticated user can view all users' shopping baskets via /api/BasketItems

candidates.title: Weak Password Hashing - MD5 Used
candidates.proof_excerpt: JWT payload shows password hash "0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500" which is MD5('admin123') - known weak hash that reverses instantly.
candidates.poc_hint: Passwords hashed with MD5 - easily cracked

facts.summary: Login endpoint at /rest/user/login accepts JSON POST with email/password fields
SQL injection in email field with ' OR 1=1-- bypasses authentication and returns admin JWT
Registration at /api/Users accepts JSON POST and allows setting role=admin via mass assignment
Password change operates via GET request with query parameters (current, new, repeat)
Password reset via POST /rest/user/reset-password requires email, answer, new, repeat
Security question for any email can be retrieved via GET /rest/user/security-question?email=
Admin security question: 'Mother's maiden name?'
Bjoern's security question: 'Name of your favorite pet?' with answer 'Zaya'
Captcha at /rest/captcha returns answer in response body (math question)
JWT uses RS256 algorithm, no exp claim, tokens never expire
JWT contains password hash, role, email, and other sensitive user data in payload
Dual auth methods supported: Authorization Bearer header and token cookie
No logout endpoint exists - token-based sessions cannot be invalidated server-side
Login endpoint shows no rate limiting headers
Reset-password endpoint shows rate limiting (x-ratelimit-limit: 100)
/api/Challenges publicly accessible without authentication
/api/Feedbacks publicly accessible without authentication
/api/BasketItems accessible with any valid JWT showing all users' basket data
Password hashes use MD5 - easily reversible
OAuth/social login endpoints not found (/rest/user/oauth returns 500)

deadends: POST /rest/user/change-password - Unexpected path error (500) - only GET requests work for password change
/rest/user/logout - Unexpected path error (500) - no logout endpoint exists
/rest/user/oauth - Unexpected path error (500) - OAuth endpoint not implemented
/rest/user/forgot-password - Unexpected path error (500) - different path needed
/api/SecurityAnswers - 401 Unauthorized - requires different authorization context
/api/Baskets - Unexpected path error (500) - API endpoint doesn't exist at this path
/api/SecurityQuestions - 500 syntax error - API exposed but malformed request causes error
JWT alg:none attack - rejected by server (RS256 properly validated)
JWT HS256 empty-key attack - rejected by server (RS256 properly validated)
Password change via POST with JSON body - Unexpected path (500)
Password change via POST with form data - Unexpected path (500)
